routes.description: Establish that religion, assessed as a broad historical and contemporary social force, produces a net balance of human flourishing through moral motivation, service, solidarity, reform, reconciliation, and meaning that outweighs harms committed in its name.
routes.successCriteria: The pro route succeeds by showing a material causal contribution from religion to durable benefits, explaining why religious harms are neither universal nor uniquely religious, and defending those benefits against claims that they are fully replaceable by secular alternatives.

motionBridge.description: Connect religion's beneficial and harmful effects to an on-balance judgment under a consistent causal standard and comparative baseline.

centralBridges.description: Show that religious belief and organization motivate material care, durable community, interfaith cooperation, and institutions that advance human welfare.
Show that religious commitments can motivate moral reform, forgiveness, peacebuilding, and reconciliation across communal divisions.
Distinguish authentic faith from fanaticism and identify political, ethnic, or ideological causes that prevent religious wrongdoing from defining religion as a whole.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how higher purpose, humility, binding obligation, hope, and self-transcendence can direct believers toward better conduct.
Explain how religious participation can coexist with democratic authority, equal liberty, interpretation, and noncoercive engagement.

routes.description: Establish that religion is not a force for good overall because supernatural authority, exclusive truth claims, and religious institutions recurrently amplify conflict, credulity, coercion, repression, and resistance to correction, while genuine benefits remain available without religion.
routes.successCriteria: The con route succeeds by tracing substantial harms to religion's distinctive doctrines or authority structures, rebutting attempts to externalize those harms, and showing that charity, solidarity, transcendence, and moral conduct do not require supernatural belief.

motionBridge.description: Show under an even-handed causal and counterfactual test that attributable harms outweigh religiously distinctive benefits or defeat the claimed net good.

centralBridges.description: Show how divine warrant, exclusive truth, and sacred identity intensify conflict, harden political disputes, and legitimize coercion or violence.
Show how unaccountable authority and insulation from evidence enable cruelty, discrimination, sexual repression, public-health obstruction, and lost freedom.
Show that charity, solidarity, courage, consolation, transcendence, and reform can arise through secular humanism and therefore do not uniquely vindicate religion.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify where religion supplies motives, permissions, identities, institutions, or escalation mechanisms rather than merely accompanying independent conflict.
Explain how church-state separation, individual autonomy, evidence-based inquiry, and nonreligious community furnish a less coercive alternative.

sections.title: Net Balance, Causal Attribution, and Secular Alternatives
sections.rationale: The motion requires a common method for attributing conduct to religion, separating religious effects from political or tribal causes, comparing benefits with harms, and testing whether claimed goods depend on faith.

sections.title: Service, Welfare, and Human Solidarity
sections.rationale: Claims about health care, relief, charity, community, and service form a principal affirmative mechanism, while the opposing burden tests their scale, distinctiveness, institutional costs, and secular replaceability.

sections.title: Conflict, Peace, and Reconciliation
sections.rationale: The debate repeatedly contests whether religion independently intensifies sectarian and territorial conflict or supplies indispensable actors, teachings, and institutions for protection, compromise, and reconciliation.

sections.title: Sacred Authority, Freedom, and Pluralism
sections.rationale: The sides dispute whether religious authority creates moral obligation within democratic limits or demands intellectual submission, coercive propagation, discrimination, and sacrifice of individual freedom.

sections.title: Scripture, Reason, and Correctability
sections.rationale: The treatment of authoritative texts determines whether harmful doctrines are intrinsic and resistant to evidence or can be constrained through historical interpretation centered on love, sacrifice, and service.

sections.title: Meaning, Transcendence, and Moral Agency
sections.rationale: Religion's proposed contributions to purpose, humility, forgiveness, and self-improvement must be compared with the claim that awe, ethics, art, and human flourishing survive without supernatural belief.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Faith-based organizations provide extensive health care, relief, and support to vulnerable people, demonstrating concrete human benefits inspired by religion.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Removing religion would not eliminate fanaticism, while authentic faith produces moral, spiritual, and emotional benefits whose absence would diminish human life.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Wrongdoing is neither universal among believers nor unique to religion, while faith also motivates valuable service that should count in an overall assessment.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Religious faith genuinely motivates compassionate service, interfaith cooperation, and substantial organized aid rather than merely attaching supernatural promises to humane conduct.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Religion can help overcome communal conflict when its cross-traditional ethic of compassion, inclusion, and service directs believers to bridge divisions.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Pluralist democracy can permit believers to participate publicly while requiring them to respect collective democratic authority and the equal freedom of others.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-002.proposition: Cooperation among Jewish, Muslim, and Christian leaders and communities can help resolve sacred disputes by fostering peace, tolerance, and shared access to holy places.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-004.proposition: Harmful scriptural literalism can be constrained through historically informed interpretation centered on love, sacrifice, and service to others.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-006.proposition: Belief in a higher power can foster humility and binding moral obligation, giving many believers a distinctive impulse toward forgiveness, peace, and self-improvement.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-001.proposition: Communism demonstrates that suppression of freedom and fanatical demands for conformity are not confined to religious faith.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-003.proposition: Faith can rationally address meaning and purpose beyond scientific explanations of life's processes while directing human will toward better conduct.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: Faith subordinates human dignity and critical judgment to a punitive supernatural authority that treats people as defective subjects commanded to satisfy an imposed plan.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: Religious credulity insulates harmful doctrines from critical judgment and can direct ordinary moral agents toward cruelty concerning punishment, sexuality, women, war, and creation.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Religious commitments materially worsen political conflict and human welfare by obstructing territorial compromise, encouraging apocalyptic politics, supporting authoritarian nationalism, and impeding effective public-health measures.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Secular measures centered on women's reproductive autonomy, education, and access to credit reliably improve poverty, health, and community welfare while religious authorities commonly resist them.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Religious charitable work cannot establish net welfare when the same religious institutions promote doctrines, such as opposition to condoms, that cause suffering charity cannot repair.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: Religion's defensible compassion, charity, and solidarity are ordinary humanist goods that do not require supernatural coercion, while religion's distinctive authority adds harms those goods cannot vindicate.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Late religious participation in Northern Ireland's peace process does not redeem centuries of violence sustained by opposed Christian identities, especially when secular dissenters resisted that division.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: American religious pluralism is secured by constitutional separation that denies government sponsorship to any faith and requires religious practice to remain voluntary rather than coercive.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Revealed religion resists confinement to peaceful private association because authoritative texts demand universal submission, encouraging imposition and proselytism beyond voluntary community.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-005.proposition: Awe, humility, transcendence, artistic achievement, and moral seriousness can survive the abandonment of supernatural belief, even though irreligion alone is not sufficient to make people good.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-007.proposition: Admirable believers and religious achievements do not establish religion's net goodness when comparable virtues occur under other movements and the doctrine demands submission to infallible authority.
